item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00455","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C23","C19","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C23","confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C23 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both directives establish a presidential commission, define its investigative and recommendation function, authorize staff outside ordinary civil-service constraints, finance the commission through a presidential appropriation with the same statutory waivers, permit earlier reports before a final report, and terminate the commission after that report. This unusually complete parallel sequence and shared administrative machinery exceed generic commission boilerplate. C19 and C22 contain similarly strong commission structures, but C23 most closely matches the child's combination and ordering of staffing, financing, reporting, and termination provisions.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"There is hereby established the President's Commission on Campaign Costs, hereinafter referred to as the Commission. The Commission shall be composed of not more than twelve members, each of whom shall be appointed by the President","parent_excerpt":"There is hereby established a Commission which shall be known as the President's Commission on Veterans' Pensions, and which shall be composed of a Chairman and six other members, all of whom shall be designated by the President.","explanation":"Both open by establishing a named President's Commission and prescribing presidential selection of its members."},{"child_excerpt":"It shall be the function of the Commission to prepare and present to the President recommendations... The Commission shall examine and inquire into, and assemble information with respect to, the costs of campaigning","parent_excerpt":"The Commission is authorized and directed to make a comprehensive survey and appraisal... and it shall make recommendations to the President regarding policies","explanation":"The operative mission in each is an information-gathering inquiry culminating in policy recommendations to the President."},{"child_excerpt":"The Commission is authorized to appoint such personnel as may be necessary... without regard to the civil service and classification laws","parent_excerpt":"Within the limits of such funds as may be made available, other persons may be employed by or under the authority of the Commission, and such employment may be without regard to the civil-service laws.","explanation":"Both confer direct staffing authority on the commission outside normal civil-service requirements."},{"child_excerpt":"Such payments shall be made without regard to the provisions of section 3681 of the Revised Statutes and section 9 of the Act of March 4, 1909","parent_excerpt":"Such payments shall be made without regard to the following: section 3681 of the Revised Statutes of the United States... section 9 of the act of March 4, 1909","explanation":"The financing provisions use the same specific statutory-waiver machinery."},{"child_excerpt":"The Commission in its discretion may transmit to the President such preliminary or interim report or reports as it may deem appropriate. It shall transmit its principal report... The Commission shall terminate not later than 120 days after","parent_excerpt":"The Commission shall make a final written report... The Commission may also make such earlier progress reports... The Commission shall cease to exist 30 days after making its final report","explanation":"Both close with the same reporting sequence—optional preliminary reports, a required principal or final report, and automatic termination afterward."}]}
